evals.name: check-reports-the-resolved-layers
evals.prompt: Is docs-naming configured in this repository?
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/setup-check.sh and presents its table as printed: the jq and git prerequisite rows, one row per configuration layer with its path and whether it is present or absent, the resolve row, the key-shape, rule, regex, tier and generated rows, and the tracked and ignored rows. Reports the exit status and changes no file.
expectations: The bundled setup-check.sh is run rather than the concern file being read and judged by hand
The table is presented with its PASS, FAIL, WARN, and INFO rows intact rather than summarized as 'configured'
A layer reported absent is explained as valid (the layer below supplies those keys), not as an error
No file is written

evals.name: check-refuses-a-malformed-layer
evals.prompt: Run the docs-naming setup check. The team layer at .claude/docs-naming.json was hand-edited this morning and now reads `{"file_names": {"regex": "^[a-z]+$"}` with no closing brace.
evals.expected_output: The check exits 1 with a FAIL on the resolve row naming .claude/docs-naming.json as invalid JSON. The response says the file must be fixed before any file-name skill runs, and does not offer to proceed with the bundled defaults instead.
expectations: The FAIL row and the named file are reported rather than a generic failure
The run is reported as exit 1, not as a warning
The remedy is fixing the named layer, never silently falling back to the bundled defaults
No file is written or repaired without the operator asking

evals.name: apply-defaults-then-verify
evals.prompt: Set up docs-naming for this repository with the bundled defaults.
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/setup-check.sh, then scripts/setup-apply.sh --defaults, then setup-check.sh again, and reports the written path .claude/docs-naming.json, the values from the second table, and that the file is still untracked and needs committing to reach the team.
expectations: apply is run through the bundled setup-apply.sh, never by composing the JSON by hand
The check is re-run after the write and the reported values come from that table
The untracked WARN is surfaced as 'commit it to share it' rather than as success
The consumer's .gitignore is not edited

evals.name: personal-layer-cannot-narrow-a-tier
evals.prompt: I put a `tiers` list in .claude/docs-naming.local.json that has only my own tier in it, but the released-changelog tier still shows up when I check. Is that a bug?
evals.expected_output: Explains that tiers is a policy-floor key: a personal layer may add entries and never remove them, because a tier decides which references the realign will rewrite in which form, and narrowing one from a single machine would weaken a team decision. Points at the check's policy-floor row and at reference/config.md, and says the remedy is to change the team layer if the tier should really go.
expectations: The behavior is named as intended, not as a defect
The reason given is that the key decides what the realign does to a tree, not merely 'that is the merge order'
The remedy offered is a team-layer change, never editing the overlay differently
generated is named as the stricter case: team layer only

evals.name: retired-team-config-name-detected-docs-naming-r001
evals.prompt: Run the docs-naming setup check. This repository still has .claude/docs-hygiene.json with a file_names block and no .claude/docs-naming.json.
evals.expected_output: Runs the retirement detection step beside the table and reports docs-naming-r001 as FAIL for .claude/docs-hygiene.json, saying the resolver still reads it for one release with a warning. The remedy is the rename (git mv .claude/docs-hygiene.json .claude/docs-naming.json), not apply with defaults. Changes no file.
expectations: check-retirements.sh is run against the plugin's retirements.yaml and its finding docs-naming-r001 is reported as FAIL
The remedy is renaming the file onto .claude/docs-naming.json, not writing a fresh file beside it
No file is changed by check

evals.name: apply-cleans-a-retired-overlay-docs-naming-r002
evals.prompt: /docs-naming:setup apply. Both .claude/docs-naming.local.json and the old .claude/docs-hygiene.local.json exist, and the old one has an exempt_paths entry the new one lacks.
evals.expected_output: Re-runs retirement detection, reports docs-naming-r002, carries only the missing exempt_paths entry into the new overlay behind a confirmation, and after the operator confirms the result runs check-retirements.sh with --clean docs-naming-r002 --i-migrated. Re-runs detection last and reports the final state.
expectations: Only the keys the new overlay lacks are added, so the new file wins
Cleanup is individually confirmed and runs --clean docs-naming-r002 --i-migrated only after the operator confirms the migrated result
The old file's content is treated as untrusted input and never executed or interpolated
Detection is re-run last and the final state is reported
